newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian bullion pulled down by world trends.
newsitem.headline: Indian bullion pulled down by world trends.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 10 rupees lower at 4,760 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,770 rupees as a fresh slide in the world market prompted profit-taking later in the day after a steady start.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 100 rupees lower at 55,700 rupees per piece after gaining 100 rupees on Wednesday.

** Silver (.999) closed 5 rupees lower at 6,870 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,875 rupees but down 10 rupees against the opening level of 6,880 rupees as fresh offerings following the subdued trend in the world market trimmed early gains towards the close.

Gold 24 carat closed 10 rupees lower at 4,760 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,770 rupees as a fresh slide in the world market prompted profit-taking later in the day after the market opened on a steady note, dealers said.
Gold was up by 5 rupees per 10 gramme on Wednesday.
Seasonal buying remained dull and volume was thin on account of poor attendance among traders due to a bank holiday to mark the birth anniversary of the Lord Buddha.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 100 rupees lower at 55,700 rupees per piece after gaining 100 rupees on Wednesday.

Silver (.999) closed 5 rupees lower at 6,870 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,875 rupees but down 10 rupees against the opening level of 6,880 rupees as the market opened higher on shortage of ready stock.
Later prices slid amid sluggish industrial buying as well as sliding global prices.
Overall market sentiment remained quiet at the close for both precious metals and physical enquiries were at low ebb. (Conversion $1=35.79 rupees)
